Question: What is the sum of all the solutions of the equation below? \[x = |2x-|60-2x||\]
Solution:
The right-hand side is nonnegative, so every solution has \(x\ge0\). At \(x=0\), the right-hand side is \(60\), so in fact \(x>0\).

An expression has absolute value \(x>0\) exactly when it equals \(x\) or \(-x\). Applying this to the outer absolute value gives two cases.

If \(2x-|60-2x|=x\), then \(|60-2x|=x\). Thus
\[60-2x=x\quad\text{or}\quad60-2x=-x,\]
which gives \(x=20\) or \(x=60\).

If \(2x-|60-2x|=-x\), then \(|60-2x|=3x\). Since \(3x>0\), this gives
\[60-2x=3x\quad\text{or}\quad60-2x=-3x.\]
The candidates are \(x=12\) and \(x=-60\). The latter is excluded by \(x>0\).

These cases cover every possible sign in both absolute values. The three positive candidates satisfy their branch equations and hence the original equation. They are distinct, so the sum of all solutions is
\[12+20+60=\boxed{92},\]
choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
